definition: Alper Yilmaz is a computer scientist and photogrammetric engineer.
details: He is a professor of civil, environmental and geodetic engineering at Ohio State University, where he holds a courtesy appointment in computer science and engineering and directs the Photogrammetric Computer Vision Laboratory. His research spans photogrammetry, computer vision, machine learning and geospatial intelligence, and he is known for his work on visual object tracking. Yilmaz served as editor-in-chief of Photogrammetric Engineering & Remote Sensing, the journal of the American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ASPRS), from 2016 to 2024, and was president of Technical Commission II (Photogrammetry) of the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ISPRS).
story: Picture walking through a crowd and instantly picking out a familiar face without reading a single name tag. The machine learns to see the way we do — starting with shapes and edges, then building up to whole objects and faces. It turns a picture into an understanding: this is a cat, that is a stop sign. Sight, for a machine, is a long climb from raw light to a name. That pixel-to-meaning climb is Alper Yilmaz.
